short: Thirteen years of conquest that carried Greek rule from the Adriatic to the Punjab.
full:
Philip II had already made Macedon master of Greece. When he was assassinated in 336 BCE his twenty-year-old son Alexander inherited an army built around the sarissa phalanx and the Companion cavalry, and a war against Persia that was already declared. He crossed into Asia in 334, destroyed the Persian field armies at Issus and Gaugamela, took Babylon, Susa and Persepolis, and pushed as far as the Hyphasis in the Punjab before his troops refused to go on.

Alexander died at Babylon in June 323 BCE, aged thirty-two, leaving no viable heir, which is why the empire is dated 336 to 323 rather than run on: as a single state it did not survive him. His generals, the Diadochi, had divided it into the Ptolemaic, Seleucid and Antigonid kingdoms within a generation of fighting. The Greek-speaking cities they founded, Alexandria above all, kept Greek as the language of government and learning from Egypt to Bactria for centuries.
